openings.claim: Fabrication candidate: two strip guides capture accessible nonworking margins, a third stops longitudinal travel, and a fourth provides a removable gate, attached through existing carriage slots. Boundary contact replaces magnetic attraction or friction. Drill strips only; bend with pliers only if section permits. Do not drill, cut, heat or glue plate/carriage; keep carriage on rails, marked 30 mm working edge exposed, and every added part outside stroke clearance.
openings.discriminator: If capture gaps plus elastic deflection remain below 1 mm, both plates should meet displacement limits despite differing magnet pull checks (7 N versus spare 3 N). Rival: bolted strip bridge pressing cork pads, dependent on preload/friction. Movement under low preload with intact capture boundaries defeats cage prediction; retention only after tightening favors friction.
openings.probe: Inspect slot access, bendability, margins and clearance with ruler; proceed only if complete capture geometry is achievable. Compare cage and cork bridge as the two configurations: at most three twenty-stroke runs and three timed removal/return checks each. Reserve final run for spare and its removal for thick gloves. Mark initial position and measure after strokes; release gate with screwdriver without touching working edge. Reject displacement above 1 mm or removal/return above sixty seconds. Stop fabrication above eighty minutes or observation above twenty minutes; incomplete comparisons remain inconclusive.
openings.uncertainty: Unknown: slots accepting supplied bolts without rail/clearance obstruction; margins capturing every escape direction; strip stiffness, achievable gaps and glove access. Three checks cannot establish dependable service performance; retention is undemonstrated.

lineage.reason: Preserves causal relation, rival/defeat tests, declared uncertain fit, constraints, stopping caveats and assumptions.

decision: Inspect feasibility first; use only supplied resources and bounded comparisons. Weak spare challenges magnetic interchangeability. Mechanical capture is discriminating but unknown attachment geometry and strip capacity prevent feasibility or performance claims.
